lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: getting ready the night before

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 2 — clothing care and readiness routines
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice getting ready the night before. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: On the night before a known day with a specific plan, the learner looks out the window or checks a simple weather note, chooses a full outfit that matches the temperature and any rain or snow, sets the outfit and shoes together on a chair or hook, and packs one bag item needed for the next day, all before going to bed and without being told to start.
safetyNotes: If checking the weather means looking outside after dark, the learner checks from a window rather than going outside alone.
If any needed item is on a shelf too high to reach safely, the learner asks a trusted adult to get it down rather than climbing on furniture.
A trusted adult confirms the finished setup only the next morning; the learner is not woken up or checked on overnight for this task.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no fixed next-day plan or the household schedule does not allow same-week testing, the learner instead plans and lays out a full outfit for a typical day on paper, listing the weather check, the outfit pieces, and the one bag item, and a trusted adult reviews the written plan instead of confirming it the next morning.

materials: learner-local: a way to check the weather, such as a window view or a simple written forecast
learner-local: a full set of clean clothing options
learner-local: a chair or hook near the door
learner-local: a bag, if one is used the next day

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one specific way this morning felt less rushed than a morning when you had to find your outfit and pack your bag after waking up.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Independence (unprompted start): The learner starts and completes the whole routine on their own, without a reminder, confirmed by the adult the next morning. | Weather-matched completeness: The full outfit, shoes, and one bag item are set out, matching the weather, and every piece is confirmed clean. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner prepare the whole routine for a two-day trip at once, laying out two full outfits and packing bag items for both days in a single night-before session.

resources.title: getting ready the night before coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: On the night before a known day with a specific plan, the learner looks out the window or checks a simple weather note, chooses a full outfit that matches the temperature and any rain or snow, sets the outfit and shoes together on a chair or hook, and packs one bag item needed for the next day, all before going to bed and without being told to start.
Coach direction: Before choosing anything, check the weather for the next day.
Learner prompt: Describe what you noticed about the weather and name the one clothing layer it makes you add or leave out.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: getting ready the night before complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Put together the whole night-before routine in order: choose the outfit, check it is clean, set it out, then pack one bag item.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I chose a full outfit that matches tomorrow's temperature and weather.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I checked that every piece of the outfit is actually clean before setting it out.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I set the outfit and shoes together on a chair or hook, not left in a pile.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I packed one item I will need for the next day into my bag.

Equal-access rule: If there is no fixed next-day plan or the household schedule does not allow same-week testing, the learner instead plans and lays out a full outfit for a typical day on paper, listing the weather check, the outfit pieces, and the one bag item, and a trusted adult reviews the written plan instead of confirming it the next morning.

resources.title: getting ready the night before minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific way this morning felt less rushed than a morning when you had to find your outfit and pack your bag after waking up.

Success checks: Independence (unprompted start): The learner starts and completes the whole routine on their own, without a reminder, confirmed by the adult the next morning. | Weather-matched completeness: The full outfit, shoes, and one bag item are set out, matching the weather, and every piece is confirmed clean.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: getting ready the night before supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional getting ready the night before condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Independence (unprompted start): The learner starts and completes the whole routine on their own, without a reminder, confirmed by the adult the next morning. | Weather-matched completeness: The full outfit, shoes, and one bag item are set out, matching the weather, and every piece is confirmed clean..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
